title: Compress Image Under 200 KB for Government Uploads
description: Government, visa, and application portals often set strict upload caps that vary by form. Set a 200 KB JPEG target in this browser-based tool and check the receiving portal's current pixel and format rules before uploading.
requirements: Max dimensions: portal-specific; enter its exact pixel limit in the resize tool if one is listed.
Accepted formats: JPEG is widely supported; confirm the destination form's allowed types.
Recommended DPI: online forms use pixel dimensions; use 300 DPI only when preparing a print or scan.

title: Resize a Passport Photo to 2 x 2 Inches
description: A 2 x 2 inch passport photo is a common US print size, while digital portals specify pixel dimensions separately. Resize locally to a 600 x 600 pixel JPEG and verify the current authority rules for your application.
requirements: Max dimensions: 600 x 600 px is a starting point for a square upload; use the portal's exact pixel range.
Accepted formats: JPEG is common for digital photo applications; check the receiving authority.
Recommended DPI: 300 DPI is a print starting point; digital acceptance depends on pixels and photo composition.

title: Compress a DV Lottery Photo Under 240 KB
description: The Diversity Visa entry workflow checks photo dimensions, file type, and composition in addition to file size. Set a 240 KB JPEG target locally in your browser, then verify the current DV Program instructions before submitting.
requirements: Max dimensions: use the exact square pixel dimensions specified by the current DV entry instructions.
Accepted formats: JPEG is the standard digital photo format; confirm current program rules.
Recommended DPI: digital checks use pixel dimensions, not DPI metadata; print resolution does not certify compliance.

title: Resize a Photo for a Schengen Visa Upload
description: Schengen visa photo guidance commonly describes a 35 x 45 mm portrait, but digital upload pixel limits vary by application center. Resize locally to 413 x 531 pixels as a proportional starting point and confirm the exact portal requirements.
requirements: Max dimensions: 413 x 531 px is a proportional 35 x 45 mm starting point at about 300 DPI, not a universal portal limit.
Accepted formats: JPEG is common for uploads; check the destination consulate or visa center.
Recommended DPI: about 300 DPI for a 35 x 45 mm print; digital forms usually validate pixels instead.

title: Convert JPG to PNG
description: Convert a JPG when an editor or upload form specifically requires PNG. This browser-based converter preserves the image dimensions, but it cannot restore detail already lost in JPG compression.
audience: People preparing images for editors and upload forms
requirements: Max dimensions: output keeps the source pixel dimensions; resize separately if a portal has a limit.
Accepted formats: JPG input and PNG output; choose PNG only when the receiving service accepts it.
Recommended DPI: conversion preserves pixel dimensions; DPI metadata is not a screen-resolution setting.

title: Convert JPG to WebP for the Web
description: WebP can reduce image payloads for sites that support the format. Convert a JPG locally, then compare the output quality and size before replacing a production asset.
requirements: Max dimensions: keep the source dimensions or resize to the actual rendered size on your page.
Accepted formats: JPG input and WebP output; verify support in the browsers and CMS you target.
Recommended DPI: DPI does not affect browser display; use enough pixels for the rendered size and device density.

title: Convert PNG to JPG for Uploads
description: Convert a PNG locally in your browser when an upload form accepts JPG but not PNG. The output uses a white background where the source has transparency, so check the preview before submitting.
audience: People preparing photos for upload forms
requirements: Max dimensions: output keeps the source pixel dimensions; resize separately to meet a portal limit.
Accepted formats: PNG input and JPEG output; transparency becomes a white background.
Recommended DPI: online forms use pixels rather than DPI; preserve enough pixels for the required display size.

title: Convert PNG to WebP for Faster Websites
description: WebP can preserve transparency while reducing many web image payloads compared with PNG. Convert locally and check visual quality, file size, and your site's browser support before publishing.
requirements: Max dimensions: resize to the rendered component size; avoid serving unnecessary source pixels.
Accepted formats: PNG input and WebP output; WebP supports transparency in modern browsers.
Recommended DPI: DPI is not used for browser rendering; optimize pixel dimensions for screen density.

title: Convert WebP to JPG for Upload Forms

audience: People preparing WebP images for uploads
requirements: Max dimensions: output keeps the source pixel dimensions; check the receiving form for limits.
Accepted formats: static WebP input and JPEG output; transparent areas become a white background.
Recommended DPI: online forms validate pixel dimensions, not DPI metadata.

title: Convert WebP to PNG
description: Convert a WebP when an editor or upload workflow requires PNG. The output keeps the source dimensions and supports transparency, but conversion cannot restore detail absent from the source.
audience: People preparing images for editors and upload forms
requirements: Max dimensions: output keeps the source pixel dimensions; resize separately if needed.
Accepted formats: static WebP input and PNG output; animated WebP is not supported.
Recommended DPI: DPI is not a screen-resolution setting; use the pixel dimensions required by your workflow.
